newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed economist sees strong Midwest growth.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed economist sees strong Midwest growth.

text.p: The Midwest econony continues to show strong growth and it appears that the auto production industry is fueling most of that strength, according to William Strauss, senior economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.
"The overall message for the February Chicago Fed Manufacturing Index (CFMMI) is one of continued strong growth here in the Midwest," Strauss said.
The CFMMI rose 1.1 percent to a record level of 125.3 in February from a revised 124.0 in January.
Strauss said that the auto sector reported strong results.
"Auto production is still up very strongly on a year-over-year basis," he said, adding that the 0.8 percent growth from last February "is still a pretty good number overall."
Looking at the Producer Price Index (PPI) data that was released earlier on Friday, Strauss noted that crude goods prices appeared to be less weaker than nine months ago.
"There has been a lot of weakness early on in terms of crude," Strauss said. Back in June 1996 crude price increases were about 15 percent below the finished good prices in the PPI, he said.
"Now that gap is less than one percent. So the situation now is certainly not the same as it was say nine months ago," Strauss added.
